summary: Peered VPC split-horizon resolves artifact host to stale private IP causing TLS certname mismatch and intermittent shard 403s
environment: prod (customer account: fin-prod, peered shared-services VPC in eu-west-1)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (FinData Labs, private deployment) reports intermittent 403 errors when Redwood serving nodes fetch large model shards (range GETs). Errors started after they created a peering connection from their application VPC into a shared-services VPC (managed by their platform team).

Impact:
- Several serving nodes intermittently fail to download shard ranges and fall back to degraded model variants.
- Customer reports visible latency spikes and increased token-cost due to retries.
- Affects production inference in eu-west-1 during peak hours; ~10% of shard downloads impacted.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC + VPCE endpoints) in eu-west-1.
- Peered to shared-services VPC (eu-west-1) with route propagation enabled into the app VPC route table.
- VPCE endpoint for artifacts uses private hostname hosted in the artifact VPC.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Trigger model load on a heavy-batch inference job that pulls sharded artifacts (range GETs).
2) Observe intermittent 403 from artifact fetcher; retry succeeds ~40% of the time.
3) Traceroute/dig from serving node sometimes returns a private IP belonging to the peered shared-services VPC rather than the artifact VPC.

Observed behavior:
- TLS handshake fails with certname mismatch in ~30% of failures (SNI host != certificate SAN).
- When TLS fails, the client receives 403 on subsequent range GET attempts (appears as application-level authorization failure).
- DNS records for artifact hostname occasionally resolve to an IP that is stale (old ENI) inside the peered VPC.

Expected behavior:
- Artifact hostname should consistently resolve to active ENI IPs in the artifact VPC/VPCE and TLS SAN should match SNI.
- No 403s caused by TLS name mismatch or stale split-horizon answers.

Attachments provided by customer:
- tcpdump + side-by-side dig results showing differing A answers between two nodes
- flow logs showing egress via the peered shared-services NAT gateway on failure traces
- short excerpt of serving node logs with TLS alert and HTTP 403 payloads
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: split-horizon DNS or route propagation caused DNS answer to point to stale ENI in peered shared-services VPC.
What we checked:
- Verified the artifact VPCE private-hostname is owned by the artifact VPC and active ENIs exist.
- Reviewed route tables: app VPC had propagated routes from peering (shared-services) that overlapped a /24 used by artifact ENIs (legacy allocation).
- AWS VPC DNS: split-horizon forwarding configured in shared-services forwarder to return internal-only addresses for the artifact hostname to on-prem/corporate forwarders.
Findings:
- During peering route propagation, some app VPC resolvers received cached/stale answers from the shared-services forwarder (it still had old A records for a decommissioned ENI).
- When a serving node resolved the artifact hostname to the stale ENI in shared-services VPC, TLS SNI sent the artifact host, but the TLS session terminated at an ALB that no longer had the correct certificate/SNI mapping for that IP -> certname mismatch.
- The ALB returned a TCP-level TLS alert in some cases; other times the intermediate proxy in shared-services accepted the connection but performed an application-layer auth check which resulted in a 403 because the request came from an unexpected source (shared-services NAT) and the authorization header check failed due to range request rewrite.
- Reproduction window correlated with TTL expiry and peering route propagation events between 02:00-03:30 UTC (their platform team applied route updates).

Intermediate conclusions:
- Root cause is a combination of stale split-horizon DNS records published by the shared-services forwarder and overlapping IP allocations across VPCs, exposed by route propagation from the peering connection.
- Secondary failure mode: request egress SNAT through shared-services NAT led to different authorization behavior for range GETs causing 403s even when TLS succeeded.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Alex Chen): Created ticket after initial customer report. Requested tcpdump, dig, and VPC flow logs.
2026-03-10 11:25 - Customer (FinData infra): Uploaded tcpdump and flow logs, noted failures started after peering and route propagation change performed by their platform team.

2026-03-10 14:02 - Support (Priya Nair): Noted correlation with route propagation. Asked customer to temporarily disable propagation into app VPC or narrow the propagated CIDR to avoid overlapping ENI block.
2026-03-11 02:45 - Customer (FinData infra): Platform team rolled back propagation; reported immediate reduction in failures. Observed issue recurred when propagation re-enabled in later window.

2026-03-11 09:30 - SRE (Priya Nair): Confirmed stale A records on shared-services DNS forwarder. Opened request with customer platform team to clear stale records and avoid overlapping IPs for artifact ENIs.
2026-03-12 08:15 - Customer (FinData infra): Cleared stale DNS entries and adjusted ENI allocation; reported no new failures in a 24h burn. Asked for recommendation to prevent recurrence.

2026-03-12 12:00 - Support (Alex Chen): Recommended follow-ups: (1) avoid overlapping CIDR/ENI allocations between peered VPCs, (2) set low TTLs on internal artifact host records during migrations, (3) use VPCE private DNS override to ensure artifact hostname resolves to artifact VPC ENIs only, (4) add route filters on propagation to limit exposed prefixes.
2026-03-12 12:04 - Customer (FinData infra): Acknowledged recommendations; will schedule change window with platform team and keep the ticket open until 7 days without regression.
resolution: Mitigation applied by customer platform team: cleared stale records from shared-services DNS forwarder, changed ENI allocation to non-overlapping CIDR, and disabled broad route propagation into app VPC. After mitigation, shard fetch failures dropped to 0% in the 24h validation window. Recommended permanent fix: enforce IP allocation boundaries for artifact VPCs and configure VPCE/private-host DNS overrides. Ticket set to monitor; pending customer confirmation after 7 days.
suggested_follow_up_items: Add automated check to detect overlapping ENI allocations across peered VPCs
Document DNS TTL best-practices for artifact migrations
Recommend VPCE private-host DNS override in runbook for private deploys
